points.title: Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property
points.summary: One of the first international intellectual property treaties. It established national treatment and the right of priority, so an applicant who files a patent or trade mark in one member country has a period to file in others with the same priority date.

points.title: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
points.summary: International agreement on copyright requiring members to protect works from other member countries without formalities such as registration, and setting minimum terms of protection for authors.

points.title: Patent Cooperation Treaty
points.summary: Lets inventors file a single international patent application that can later be pursued in many countries. It includes an international search and an optional preliminary examination before national phase entry.

points.title: Madrid Protocol on the international registration of marks
points.summary: Allows trade mark owners to seek protection in many countries through one application filed with their home office and administered by WIPO.

points.title: Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
points.summary: World Trade Organization agreement setting minimum standards for patents, copyright, trade marks, designs and other IP that member countries must provide, with dispute settlement for enforcement.

points.title: WIPO Copyright Treaty
points.summary: Updated international copyright rules for the digital environment, covering computer programs, databases and the legal protection of technological measures that restrict copying.

points.title: Diamond v. Chakrabarty
points.summary: United States Supreme Court decision holding that a genetically modified bacterium capable of breaking down crude oil was patentable subject matter, opening the way for biotechnology patents.

points.title: Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International
points.summary: United States Supreme Court decision that claims to an abstract idea implemented on a generic computer are not patent eligible, reshaping the examination of software and business method patents.

points.title: D'Arcy v Myriad Genetics
points.summary: High Court of Australia decision that isolated genetic material coding for the BRCA1 gene was not a patentable invention, because the substance of the claim was genetic information rather than a manner of manufacture.

points.title: Commissioner of Patents v Thaler (DABUS)
points.summary: The Full Federal Court of Australia held that an inventor named on a patent application must be a natural person, overturning an earlier ruling that the AI system DABUS could be named as an inventor.

points.title: Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service
points.summary: United States Supreme Court decision that facts are not protected by copyright and that a telephone directory's white pages lacked the minimal creativity needed for protection.

points.title: Authors Guild v. Google
points.summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit found that Google's scanning of books to create a searchable index with short snippets was fair use.

points.title: Creative Commons licences released
points.summary: The first set of Creative Commons licences gave creators a simple, standardised way to grant the public permission to share and reuse their work on stated conditions.

points.title: Attention Is All You Need
points.summary: Research paper introducing the transformer, a neural network architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms that became the foundation of modern large language models.

points.title: Efficient estimation of word representations in vector space (word2vec)
points.summary: Introduced simple neural models that learn vector representations of words from large text corpora, where words with similar meanings end up close together.

points.title: BERT: pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers
points.summary: Research paper describing BERT, a language model pre-trained on unlabelled text that reads context in both directions and can be fine-tuned for many language tasks. Its architecture underlies many sentence embedding models.

points.title: Visualizing data using t-SNE
points.summary: Paper introducing t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, a technique for visualising high-dimensional data in two or three dimensions that is particularly good at revealing clusters.

points.title: UMAP: uniform manifold approximation and projection
points.summary: Paper describing UMAP, a dimension reduction technique grounded in topology that is fast and tends to preserve more global structure than t-SNE.

points.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
points.summary: Research paper reporting that the AlphaFold system predicts the three-dimensional structure of proteins with accuracy competitive with experimental methods.

points.title: ChatGPT released to the public
points.summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT, a conversational assistant built on a large language model, which reached a very large audience within weeks and prompted wide debate about generative AI.

points.title: European Parliament approves the Artificial Intelligence Act
points.summary: The European Parliament voted to adopt the AI Act, which regulates artificial intelligence systems according to their level of risk and sets transparency duties for general-purpose models.

points.title: Paris Agreement
points.summary: International climate agreement in which countries committed to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, through nationally determined contributions reviewed over time.

points.title: Kyoto Protocol
points.summary: International treaty that committed industrialised countries to binding targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, with market mechanisms such as emissions trading.

points.title: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
points.summary: Treaty phasing out chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting chemicals. It is widely regarded as one of the most successful environmental agreements.

points.title: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report: synthesis report
points.summary: Summarises the scientific assessment of climate change, its impacts and options for adaptation and mitigation, concluding that rapid and deep emissions cuts are needed this decade.

points.title: Garnaut Climate Change Review final report
points.summary: Independent review commissioned by Australian governments examining the impacts of climate change on the Australian economy and recommending an emissions trading scheme.

points.title: On the antibacterial action of cultures of a Penicillium
points.summary: Alexander Fleming's paper reporting that a mould contaminating a bacterial culture produced a substance that killed bacteria, later developed into penicillin.

points.title: A programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease (CRISPR-Cas9)
points.summary: Showed that the Cas9 enzyme can be programmed with guide RNA to cut DNA at chosen sites, laying the groundwork for CRISPR genome editing.

points.title: Unidentified curved bacilli in the stomach of patients with gastritis
points.summary: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren reported bacteria in the stomachs of patients with gastritis and peptic ulcers, work later recognised with the Nobel Prize.

points.title: Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine receives first authorisation
points.summary: The United Kingdom's medicines regulator gave the first emergency authorisation of an mRNA vaccine against COVID-19.

points.title: Human Genome Project declared complete
points.summary: The international project announced it had sequenced essentially the whole human genome, providing a reference used across biology and medicine.

points.title: James Webb Space Telescope launched
points.summary: The largest space telescope yet launched, designed for infrared astronomy to observe the earliest galaxies, star formation and the atmospheres of exoplanets.

points.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
points.summary: The first crewed Moon landing: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module and walked on the surface, with images relayed through stations including Parkes in Australia.

points.title: Australian Space Agency begins operations
points.summary: Australia established a national space agency to coordinate civil space activity and grow the domestic space industry.

points.title: First image of a black hole
points.summary: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first image of a black hole's shadow, at the centre of the galaxy M87.

points.title: Mapping Global Trade in Fakes 2025
points.summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. OECD–EUIPO analysis estimates that counterfeit and pirated goods represented up to 2.3% of global trade in 2021. Published in 2025 but based on 2021 customs seizure data, it provides an updated international enforcement benchmark rather than a current Australian market estimate. Strategic implication: explore customs intelligence partnerships and risk-based SME support; do not use these global figures to extrapolate Australia's counterfeit market or validate the 2022 growth assumption.

points.title: Amazon's Trustworthy Shopping Experience Report 2025
points.summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem; Amplify Australian IP. Amazon reports that proactive controls blocked more than 99.9% of suspected infringing listings before brand owners needed to report them, and that more than 15 million counterfeit products were identified, seized and disposed of during 2025. Its tools combine brand registration, infringement reporting, product serialisation and direct removal capabilities. Strategic implication: examine platform partnerships and practical SME onboarding support, while treating company-reported results as platform-specific evidence rather than independent measures of Australian coverage.

points.title: UK Intellectual Property Office mediation service
points.summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. The UK IPO offers mediation covering patents, trade marks, designs, copyright, trade secrets and related commercial matters, including online sessions. Both parties must agree to participate. Strategic implication: a comparator for affordable post-registration dispute support, including referral partnerships, online delivery and transparent pricing; evaluate suitability, settlement outcomes and participation barriers rather than assuming mediation can replace enforcement. The publication date is the guidance page's original publication date, not the commencement date of every current service feature.

points.title: Australian IP Report 2026: productivity and income research
points.summary: Territories: Empower others; Amplify Australian IP. IP Australia reports that businesses registering their first trade mark experienced an average 16% increase in sales per worker compared with equivalent businesses on similar growth paths without protection; first patent grants were associated with a 15% increase in overall efficiency. Strategic implication: develop evidence-based outreach linking suitable IP protection to business outcomes, while avoiding promises that registration alone will produce these gains for individual SMEs.

points.title: Australian IP Report 2025: examination timing and commercialisation
points.summary: Territories: Empower others; Amplify Australian IP. The report discusses research indicating that small innovators engaging with IP early can benefit from influencing examination timing, with implications for innovation, commercialised products and lifetime IP value. Strategic implication: investigate customer-controlled timing and guidance that align protection with experimentation, funding and market entry, rather than treating faster examination as universally preferable. Publication year: 2025; an exact publication date was not established from the retrieved source.

points.title: EUIPO SME Fund 2025
points.summary: Territories: Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. EUIPO reports that the sixth edition of its SME Fund launched on 3 February 2025 through collaboration with the European Commission and European Union Intellectual Property Network, providing financial support for SME intellectual property protection. Strategic implication: examine targeted financial assistance delivered through partner networks as a comparator for reducing Australian SME cost barriers. Assess additional uptake, application quality and commercial usefulness rather than registration volumes alone. The date records the announcement's publication.

points.title: UK IP Advance grant funding
points.summary: Territories: Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. UK government guidance identifies IP Advance as a scheme supporting innovative SMEs with intellectual property, including copyright, designs, trade marks and patents. Strategic implication: examine the scheme as a comparator for assistance spanning different IP assets rather than a single registration pathway, and investigate eligibility, delivery partners and outcomes before considering Australian adaptation.

points.title: WIPO IP Finance Dialogue 2025: The Value of Intangible Assets
points.summary: Territories: Amplify Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. WIPO's dialogue brought together issues of IP valuation, recognition, disclosure and access to capital, highlighting the need to build lender and investor trust in intangible assets. Strategic implication: explore common IP information templates, valuation literacy and partnerships with financiers and valuation professionals; distinguish an asset's estimated commercial value from its acceptability as loan collateral. The date is the dialogue date rather than a verified webpage publication date.

points.title: UK Intellectual Property Office Corporate Plan 2025 to 2026
points.summary: Territories: Amplify Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. The plan identifies engagement with industry to help innovative SMEs leverage IP assets to access finance and commits to publishing an IP finance annual report. Strategic implication: an institutional comparator for an IP office extending beyond registration through evidence development and finance-sector engagement, without assuming that the office must itself become a lender or valuation provider. Publication year: 2025; an exact publication date was not established from the retrieved source.

points.title: Australian IP Report 2026: research programme and IP First Response
points.summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem; Empower others. The research programme records progress during 2025 on IP First Response, a pilot digital service assisting both SMEs facing suspected infringement and businesses accused of infringement. Strategic implication: design post-registration support around both sides of disputes, with proportionate triage and referral pathways rather than rights-holder enforcement alone. This is evidence of service development, not proof of reduced dispute costs or improved outcomes. Publication year: 2026; an exact chapter publication date was not established.

points.title: Australian IP Report 2026: Indigenous business research partnerships
points.summary: Territories: Cultivate our ecosystem; Revisit our purpose; Amplify Australian IP. IP Australia's research programme identifies collaboration with the University of Melbourne's Dilin Duwa Centre for Indigenous Business Leadership to examine the commercial value of trade marks for Indigenous businesses and the potential economic role of trade marks containing Indigenous Knowledge. Strategic implication: use Indigenous-led research partnerships to test whose value is recognised and how services support Indigenous economic participation, without reducing cultural value to registration or financial metrics. Publication year: 2026; an exact chapter publication date was not established.

points.title: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
points.summary: Territories: Revisit our purpose; Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. Adopted on 24 May 2024, the treaty establishes a patent disclosure framework concerning genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge. WIPO explains that the disclosure requirement operates upon entry into force following ratification by 15 contracting parties. Strategic implication: examine provenance information, applicant guidance and engagement with Indigenous Peoples; do not describe adoption alone as creating an operative Australian disclosure obligation or comprehensive Indigenous Knowledge protection. The date is the treaty's adoption date.

points.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability
points.summary: Territories: Revisit our purpose; Empower others; Amplify Australian IP. The US Copyright Office concludes that generative AI outputs can receive copyright protection where a human determines sufficient expressive elements, but not merely through providing prompts; AI assistance does not itself disqualify a work. Strategic implication: distinguish human contribution, ownership and protectability when developing AI-related guidance and assessing commercial IP value. This is a US legal-policy position, not a statement of Australian copyright law.

points.title: IP Australia Strategic Corporate Plan 2026–27
points.summary: Territories: Revisit our purpose; Cultivate our ecosystem; Empower others. IP Australia's announcement identifies AI governance and accountability, First Nations engagement and economic empowerment, and improved services, education and guidance as priorities. Strategic implication: use these commitments as a current alignment framework for horizon initiatives, particularly responsible AI-enabled assistance, inclusive service design and partnership proposals. The date records the announcement's publication.

points.title: Australian IP Report 2026: structural shifts in international IP activity
points.summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. IP Australia reports that Australian resident trade mark filings increased 15% in 2025, applications originated from 138 locations, and Australian resident patent filings increased 9%, alongside declining US-linked international patent collaboration and increasing Chinese-origin activity in applied and industrial technologies. Strategic implication: reassess priority markets, overseas protection guidance and partner networks using changing filing patterns; filings indicate system use, not infringement incidence or proof of commercial success.
